q1: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2: SELECT DISTINCT V1.VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS V1 JOIN VIEWS V2 WHERE V1.VIEWER_ID = V2.VIEWER_ID AND V1.VIEW_DATE = V2.VIEW_DATE AND V1.ARTICLE_ID != V2.ARTICLE_ID ORDER BY V1.VIEWER_ID
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT V1.VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS V1 JOIN VIEWS V2 WHERE V1.VIEWER_ID = V2.VIEWER_ID AND V1.VIEW_DATE = V2.VIEW_DATE AND V1.ARTICLE_ID != V2.ARTICLE_ID ORDER BY V1.VIEWER_ID
counterexample: INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (1, 101, 201, '2023-01-01');
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 groups by VIEW_DATE and VIEWER_ID, and selects viewers who have viewed more than one distinct article on that specific date. Q2, on the other hand, uses a join to find viewers who have viewed at least two different articles on the same date, regardless of whether the articles are distinct or not.
counterexample_dsp: A viewer who views the same article multiple times on the same date.
